findings.reason: The old chart injected ms-secret-vault via envFrom (charts/templates/deployment.yaml:76-78), and that secret comes from the Vault ExternalSecret (k8s-configs/eos-microservice.yaml:12). The new container has only five literal env vars and no envFrom. The mounted ConfigMap (backend/ai-secure-agent-config.yaml:14) sets MySQL user root with no password. Once agent-app syncs, the pod starts without the credentials it had before, so high is justified (X1 said medium).
findings.claim: The new Deployment drops the envFrom secretRef to ms-secret-vault, so the agent loses its Vault-supplied credentials.
findings.evidence: The old Helm path rendered `envFrom: - secretRef: name: {{ .Values.externalSecret.targetName | default "ms-secret-vault" }}` (charts/templates/deployment.yaml:76-78). That secret is created by the ExternalSecret in k8s-configs/eos-microservice.yaml from `secret/ceramicraft`. The new manifest's `env:` block (lines 31-41) lists only CONFIG_PATH, PYTHONUNBUFFERED, ENABLE_MLFLOW_TRACING, MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI and MALLOC_ARENA_MAX, and it has no `envFrom`. The mounted config (backend/ai-secure-agent-config.yaml:14) sets `username: "root"` for MySQL with no password. Every other service in the repo gets its password from the secret env. So once agent-app syncs, the pod connects to MySQL as root with no password.

members.claim: Removing readiness and liveness probes allows an unready or hung agent process to remain a Service endpoint without automatic recovery.

If the process remains running while its HTTP handler is unhealthy, no remaining application health check removes it from endpoints or restarts it.
